edition.locus: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR (sources/canones_GR.pdf), p. 2, Canon ζ´

source_text: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν ἐγκαταλεχθέντας τοῖς βαρβάροις καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας, ἐπιλαθομένους ὅτι ἦσαν Ποντικοὶ καὶ χριστιανοὶ, ἐκβαρβαρωθέντας δὲ ὡς καὶ φονεύειν τοὺς ὁμοφύλους ἢ ξύλῳ ἢ ἀγχόνῃ, ὑποδεικνῦναι δὲ ἢ ὁδοὺς ἢ οἰκίας ἀγνοοῦσι τοῖς βαρβάροις, καὶ τῆς ἀκροάσεως ἀπεῖρξαι δεῖ, μέχρις ἂν κοινῇ περὶ αὐτῶν τι δόξῃ συνελθοῦσι, τοῖς ἁγίοις, καὶ πρὸ αὐτῶν τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι.
thought_title: Those who joined the invaders against their own people
orientation: Christians who joined the raiders and helped them kill or rob their own people are barred even from the hearers until the gathered saints decide their case.
pass_a_gloss: Those then enrolled among the barbarians and with them in the captivity having attacked, having forgotten that they were Pontics and Christians, having been made barbarian so as even to kill those of the same race either by wood or by strangling/noose, and to point out either roads or houses to the barbarians not knowing [them], it is necessary to shut them out even from the hearing, until in common something about them seems good to the saints having come together, and before them to the Holy Spirit.

choices.english: while captives, joined them in their attacks
choices.why: Read as Pontic captives who were enlisted and then joined the raiders' attacks.
rejected: attacked with them in the captivity

choices.why: The penitential grade of the hearers described in Canon 11.

choices.english: seems good ... to the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Keeps the Acts 15:28 formula visible and does not make the Holy Spirit the grammatical subject of a decision.
rejected: until the Holy Spirit reaches a decision

bible_refs.note: ἔδοξε ... τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, the council formula of Acts 15:28 with the order reversed; a clear echo, not a quotation

pass_b_english: Some were enlisted among the barbarians and, while captives, joined them in their attacks, forgetting that they were men of Pontus and Christians, and became so barbarous as even to kill their own countrymen with a club or a noose, and to show roads or houses to the barbarians who did not know them. These must be barred even from the stage of hearing, until a decision about them seems good in common to the saints when they have met together, and, before them, to the Holy Spirit (Acts 15:28).
notes: Rubric left out (editorial). ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας is ambiguous ('attacked with them in the captivity'); read as Pontic captives who were enlisted and then joined the raiders' attacks, so 'while captives, joined them in their attacks'. ξύλῳ rendered 'with a club'; it could also mean a gallows or stake (ANF 'gibbet'); ἀγχόνη = noose, strangling. ἀκρόασις is the penitential grade of the hearers (see section 11), so 'the stage of hearing'. The closing words echo the council formula of Acts 15:28 (ἔδοξε τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι καὶ ἡμῖν), with the order reversed by 'before them'; cited as a clear allusion, not a quotation; the English keeps 'seems good to … the Holy Spirit' so the echo stays visible. Χριστιανοί printed lower-case in the source; 'Christians' capitalised as English requires. κοινῇ correction follows the source note.
drafter: claude (Claude Code, Opus); Cloudflare AI off

changes: closing clause rewritten: the Holy Spirit was grammatically made to 'reach a decision'; now 'until a decision about them seems good in common to the saints … and, before them, to the Holy Spirit', matching δόξῃ … τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι and the Acts 15:28 echo

assembly (structural gate only): the one long sentence was split at the dash before 'these must be barred' ('As for those who ... and who became' -> 'Some were ... and became ... . These must be barred'); no clause added or dropped
